question: Is the CMVP-validated module the same product (or the cryptographic module of the same product line and hardware/major release) as the Common Criteria certified product? Verdicts use only the attributes shown in both lists (vendor, product designation, hardware list, release, dates).

pairs.cmvp_module: u.trust Anchor
pairs.reason: Same product: u.trust Anchor HSM from the same vendor; CC row is a later release (4.49.1, 2025) of the module validated in 2022.

pairs.cmvp_module: SUSE Linux Enterprise Libgcrypt Cryptographic Module
pairs.reason: Shared tokens are only 'linux enterprise': the CMVP row is a Libgcrypt module with no product version, the CC row is SLE Micro 5.3; not the same product.

pairs.cmvp_module: Cisco Catalyst 3560-X and 3750-X Switches
pairs.reason: Different hardware: Catalyst 3560-X/3750-X (validated 2011) vs Catalyst 9400X/9600X (certified 2024).

pairs.cmvp_module: McAfee Firewall Enterprise Control Center Virtual Appliance
pairs.cc_name: McAfee Firewall Enterprise v8.2.0 and McAfee Firewall Enterprise Control Center v5.2.0
pairs.reason: Same product line: Firewall Enterprise Control Center is part of the CC evaluated configuration (Control Center v5.2.0); the CMVP validation (2015) is of a later release, version not shown in the list.

pairs.cmvp_module: EnCase Enterprise Cryptographic Module
pairs.reason: Same product: EnCase Enterprise, CMVP module validated 2008-05 and CC certificate for version 6.8 issued 2008-11.

pairs.cmvp_module: SafeGuard Easy
pairs.reason: Same product: SafeGuard Easy by the same vendor (CC 2004 for version 3.20, CMVP 2006); releases differ.

pairs.cmvp_module: Palo Alto Networks SD-WAN Instant-On Network (ION) Devices ION 1200, ION 1200-S, ION 3200, ION 5200, and ION 9200
pairs.cc_name: Palo Alto Networks SD-WAN Instant-On Network (ION) Devices ION 1200, ION 1200-S, ION 3200, ION 5200, ION 9200, vION, and Controller running 6.5
pairs.reason: Same product: SD-WAN ION devices, identical hardware list (ION 1200, 1200-S, 3200, 5200, 9200) in both records.

pairs.cmvp_module: VPN Firewall Brick® 350 and Brick® 1000
pairs.reason: Same product line: the Brick 350/1000 are the Lucent VPN Firewall appliances; CC certificate covers VPN Firewall V7.2 (2006), CMVP 2004.

pairs.cmvp_module: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6.2 OpenSSH Server Cryptographic Module
pairs.reason: Different major release: RHEL 6.2 OpenSSH module (2012) vs RHEL 9.4 (2025).

pairs.cmvp_module: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6.6 NSS Module
pairs.reason: Different major release: RHEL 6.6 NSS module (2016) vs RHEL 9.4 (2025).

pairs.cmvp_module: Nexus 7000 Series Switches
pairs.cc_name: Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches Running NX-OS 10.4
pairs.reason: Different hardware family: Nexus 7000 (2014) vs Nexus 9000 (2025).

pairs.cmvp_module: SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 12 SP2 - NSS Cryptographic Module
pairs.cc_name: SUSE Linux Enterprise Server Version 15 SP2
pairs.reason: Different release: SLES 12 SP2 NSS module vs SLES 15 SP2; the shared 'sp2' is coincidental.

pairs.cmvp_module: FastIron ICX™ 7750, ICX™ 7250 and ICX™ 7150 Series Switch/Router
pairs.cc_name: CommScope Technologies LLC, Ruckus FastIron ICX Series Switch/Router 10.0.10
pairs.reason: Same product line: FastIron ICX switch/router series (CMVP lists ICX 7750/7250/7150, CC lists the ICX series on FastIron 10.0.10); individual models not listed in the CC row.

pairs.cmvp_module: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Libreswan Cryptographic Module v4.0
pairs.reason: Different major release: Libreswan module for RHEL 7-era (2016) vs RHEL 9.4 (2025).

pairs.cmvp_module: Cisco Catalyst 9200L Series Switches
pairs.reason: Same product: Catalyst 9200L switches are in the CC row (Catalyst 9200/9200L, IOS-XE 17.18); CMVP validation 2023, CC 2026.

pairs.cmvp_module: Cisco Secure Access Control Server (ACS) FIPS module (cryptolib)
pairs.cc_name: Cisco Nexus 7000 Series Switch running Software version NX-OS version 5.1(a) and Cisco Secure Access Control Server (ACS) running version 5.2 patch 3
pairs.reason: Same product: Cisco Secure ACS is named in the CC evaluated configuration (ACS 5.2 patch 3, certified 2011-04); CMVP module validated 2011-02.

pairs.cmvp_module: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6.2 Libgcrypt Cryptographic Module
pairs.reason: Different major release: RHEL 6.2 Libgcrypt module (2012) vs RHEL 9.4 (2025).

pairs.cmvp_module: CRATON2/SECTON embedded V2X HSM
pairs.cc_name: SECTON / CRATON2 Embedded V2X HSM CUT3.1
pairs.reason: Same product: CRATON2/SECTON embedded V2X HSM in both records (CMVP 2022, CC 2023).

pairs.cmvp_module: AirFortress Wireless Security Gateway Cryptographic Module
pairs.reason: Not confirmable: AirFortress Wireless Security Gateway module (2002) vs Fortress Wireless Secure Gateway Version 1.0 (2007); different product designation and five years apart.

pairs.cmvp_module: McAfee Firewall Enterprise Control Center Virtual Appliance
pairs.cc_name: McAfee Firewall Enterprise v8.2.0 and McAfee Firewall Enterprise Control Center v5.2.0
pairs.reason: Same product: Firewall Enterprise Control Center, CMVP validated 2012-10 and CC certificate (Control Center v5.2.0) 2012-01.

declared_join_spot_check.note: The 16 CMVP certificate numbers cited in the 11 sampled Security Targets were each read against the CMVP row (join_cmvp_number_cited_in_st.hits). In 14 the cited sentence names the same module or product as the CMVP row (e.g. #1747 OpenSSL FIPS Object Module, #2241 Cisco 5915 and 5940 Embedded Services Routers, #989 Windows XP Enhanced Cryptographic Provider); in 2 (#3043, #784) the sentence does not name the module and only the vendor lineage agrees. Cited modules are often a third party's library embedded in the product, so the link means 'uses or embeds this validated module', not 'is this module'.
